oem_wiki_description: Suzuki Motor Corporation is a Japanese multinational mobility manufacturer headquartered in Hamamatsu, Shizuoka Prefecture. It manufactures automobiles, motorcycles, all-terrain vehicles (ATVs), outboard marine engines, wheelchairs and a variety of other small internal combustion engines. In 2016, Suzuki was the eleventh biggest automaker by production worldwide.

oem_wiki_description: Tata Motors Limited is an Indian multinational automotive manufacturer headquartered in Mumbai, Maharashtra, and is a core company of the Tata Group conglomerate. It produces a wide range of vehicles including passenger cars, sport utility vehicles (SUVs), pick-ups, trucks, buses and electric vehicles, and has a significant presence in both the passenger and commercial vehicle segments in India and abroad. \n - Founded in 1945, Tata Motors has expanded into international markets and today serves customers in well over 100 countries through its network of subsidiaries, joint ventures and distribution partners. The company is recognized as one of India’s leading automakers by volume and has played a key role in the country’s shift toward safer and more sustainable mobility, especially through its fast-growing electric vehicle portfolio

It is a vertically integrated company with several major subsidiaries, including BYD Auto which produces automobiles, BYD Electronics which produces electronic parts and assembly, and FinDreams, a brand name of multiple companies that produce automotive components and electric vehicle batteries.

oem_wiki_description: Kia Corporation is a South Korean multinational automobile manufacturer headquartered in Seoul, South Korea. Founded in 1944, it is South Korea’s oldest motor vehicle manufacturer and operates as a key subsidiary of the Hyundai Motor Group. Kia manufactures a wide range of vehicles including passenger cars, SUVs, MPVs, commercial vehicles, and electric vehicles, with a strong global focus on design, technology, and electrification. As of the early 2020s, Kia ranks among the top global automakers by production and sales, with operations and sales spanning 190+ markets worldwide.

oem_wiki_description: Hyundai Motor Company is a South Korean multinational automotive manufacturer headquartered in Seoul, South Korea. Founded in 1967, it manufactures passenger cars, SUVs, commercial vehicles, and electric and hydrogen fuel-cell vehicles. Hyundai operates production and R&D facilities worldwide and is a core subsidiary of Hyundai Motor Group. It consistently ranks among the world’s largest automakers by global vehicle sales.

oem_wiki_description: Mahindra & Mahindra Limited is an Indian multinational automotive manufacturing company headquartered in Mumbai, Maharashtra. Founded in 1945, it produces passenger vehicles, utility vehicles, commercial vehicles, tractors, and electric vehicles. Mahindra is a flagship company of the Mahindra Group and is one of India’s largest automobile manufacturers, with a strong presence in SUVs, tractors, and off-road vehicles, along with operations in multiple international markets.

oem_wiki_description: The Ford Motor Company is an American multinational automotive manufacturer headquartered in Dearborn, Michigan, United States. Founded in 1903, it designs, manufactures, and sells passenger cars, trucks, SUVs, commercial vehicles, and electric vehicles under the Ford and Lincoln brands. Ford operates manufacturing and R&D facilities worldwide and is one of the world’s largest automakers by global vehicle sales.

oem_wiki_description: General Motors Company is an American multinational automotive manufacturer headquartered in Detroit, Michigan, United States. Founded in 1908, it produces passenger cars, trucks, SUVs, commercial vehicles, and electric vehicles under brands including Chevrolet, GMC, Cadillac, and Buick. GM operates globally with significant manufacturing and technology operations and consistently ranks among the world’s largest automakers by vehicle sales.

oem_brand_awareness: High global brand awareness; Fortune 500 technology company with operations in over 170 countries and annual revenue exceeding $50 billion
oem_wiki_description: Hewlett-Packard Incorporated is an American multinational information technology corporation headquartered in Palo Alto, California. Founded in 1939 by Bill Hewlett and Dave Packard, it developed into one of the world's largest technology companies, producing personal computers, printers, servers, and imaging solutions. In 2015, the company split into two independent entities: HP Inc. and Hewlett Packard Enterprise.

oem_wiki_description: Yamaha Motor Corporation is a Japanese multinational mobility manufacturer headquartered in Iwata, Shizuoka, Japan. Founded in 1955, it manufactures motorcycles, motorboats, outboard motors, recreational vehicles, personal watercraft, marine engines, golf carts, and ATVs. Yamaha is the world's second-largest motorcycle manufacturer and the global leader in water vehicle sales.

oem_wiki_description: Honda Motor Corporation is a leading Japanese manufacturer of motorcycles and a major producer of automobiles for the world market, headquartered in Tokyo. Founded by Soichiro Honda in 1948, it began producing motorcycles in 1949 and has been the top-selling motorcycle company in the world since 1959.

oem_wiki_description: Mercedes-Benz Group AG is a German multinational automotive company headquartered in Stuttgart, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. The company produces luxury passenger cars, SUVs, commercial vehicles, buses, and electric mobility solutions under the Mercedes-Benz brand. Mercedes-Benz is globally known for pioneering automotive technologies, premium engineering, advanced safety systems, and high-performance vehicles including AMG and Maybach lineups.

oem_wiki_description: MG Motor (Morris Garages) is a British automotive marque founded by Cecil Kimber in Oxford, UK in 1924, now owned by Chinese state-owned enterprise SAIC Motor Corporation. Originally known for iconic British sports cars, the brand underwent multiple ownership changes through British Motor Corporation, British Leyland, and Rover Group before being acquired by Nanjing Automobile Group in 2005, which subsequently merged into SAIC Motor in 2007. Today, MG operates globally with design studios in Shanghai and London, producing SUVs, electric vehicles, and AI-powered cars.
